segments.text: 21 life skills — if you learn them, they will give you a huge advantage
over others.
These are the skills
that will help you move ahead in life. Let’s quickly start. Skill
No. 1 – **Ability
to Focus** Look, today’s world is full of distractions.
Everyone wants just one thing from you — **your attention**.
And people are spending millions and billions of rupees to get it.
They are spending a lot of their energy just to grab your attention.
But this attention — you might think it’s free — is actually **not free**.
When you take your focus away from your goals and your own priorities and give it
to others, it means you are saying **NO** to your goals, your dreams, and your
life. That’s why it’s very important to learn how to focus in your life.
Otherwise, if you stay distracted, your “monkey mind”
will just keep jumping from one thing to another.
You’ll keep jumping from one video to another, and this video is my challenge
to you — watch it till the very end with full focus.
Developing focus can start with a simple exercise: whatever you
are doing, immerse yourself completely in it and do only that one thing.
Do it for a long stretch of time. This is how your focus will develop.
That’s why don’t watch this video just as a video — watch it as a challenge.
Through this video, you are not only learning about skills
but also training your “focus muscle.” If you want
to improve your focus even more, you can read this book.
The next
skill is **discipline**. Look, anyone can do something powerful once, but being
able to do the same thing again and again with discipline is not something everyone
can do. This
is exactly what differentiates the **top 1%** from the remaining 99%. The 99% are
always chasing dopamine — novelty, something new, some fresh excitement —
just like many people who might be watching this video right now.
They also probably want to know about some new skills, to learn something new.
But the truth is, success comes when you **repeat the boring things**. When
you are ready to do the same thing you have already done 100 times — for the
101st time as well. Most people work only when they feel like it, but
those who have discipline work **whether they feel like it or not**.
And these are the people who are able to achieve their dreams. If you want
to build discipline, here’s one of my favorite books that you can read.
The next skill is **selling** — this is the one skill that can help you earn a
lot of money in the least amount of time. Look, technology will keep changing.
People will keep changing. Times will keep changing.
Products will keep changing. But a person who
knows how to sell will always survive by selling something or the other.
In fact, do you know that almost all millionaires and billionaires
have done selling at some point in their lives?
Some millionaires have sold newspapers, some have done network marketing
— and if you notice, almost every millionaire or billionaire has been able
to reach where
they are **because at some point in their life, they have done selling**.
The next skill
is **deep work**. Look, there are two ways of working: One is **shallow
work** — where you are just working for the sake of working, just passing time.
And the other is **deep work** — where you are so immersed in what you’re doing
that you lose track
of time, you don’t even realize how many hours or minutes have passed.
When you can’t even keep count of the time, that is what we call **deep work**,
which Cal Newport talks about in his book. This deep work is often achieved
when you enter a **flow state**. You might have noticed this yourself — many
times when you are playing a game, you get into a flow state. Many doctors
also experience a flow state when they are performing surgeries.
Many musicians also enter a flow state when they play their instruments, and when
they are in that flow — in that deep work state — that’s when they are able
to give their **best performance**.
That’s why it’s important to learn this skill too. The next skill you need
to learn in life is **communication**. Because sooner or later, you will have
to deal with people.
If you create a product, you will have to sell it to people. If you want to run
a company, you will have to deal with people in your company. And whenever
you have to deal with people, you will need one thing — **good communication**.
I believe communication
is simply the ability to express your ideas and feelings clearly.
There’s a very beautiful lesson I learned from the book **How to Win Friends and
Influence People**, and I want to share it with you. If you want to communicate
well, always **seek first to understand, then to
be understood**. When you genuinely think about others’ well-being and
have good intentions, you will automatically be able
to communicate better. The next skill is **patience** —
the ability to stay calm and wait. There are two types of people… One group runs
after **instant gratification**, and the other understands the power
of **delayed gratification**. People who chase instant gratification
always want something
**right now** —
they want an immediate dopamine rush.
If they are investing money, they expect instant returns.
Because of this mindset, such people often get heavily involved in betting apps,
trading, and similar things — thinking, “I’ll just put my money
in right now and get quick returns.”
They think, “The chart will move a little here and there,
and I’ll become rich.” You might have seen the **Marshmallow Test**
video — it teaches us the same thing: The child
who can delay their gratification, even for a little while, is the one who
grows and succeeds in life. And you’ll notice this trait in every successful
person. Even businessmen don’t create businesses just for today…
They create businesses while thinking 5 to 10
years ahead. A laborer wants to be paid **today itself**, which is why
they earn less. But a builder gets paid much later and has to take on a
lot of risk — but the reward they receive is the highest. You’ll notice this
in every field: **delayed gratification always gives you the best results.**
But this ability to delay gratification will only come from one skill —
**patience**. The next skill, and one of my favorites, is **storytelling**.
If I ask you to recall your 10th-grade board exams — the ones you probably worked
so hard for — and share with me anything you still remember from history
or geography lessons, there’s a very small chance you’ll actually remember much.
But if I ask you whether you’ve ever heard the story of **the
hare and the tortoise** — a story you might have heard 10 or 15 years ago —
you’d probably still remember it even today, right? That’s because
our brain is **wired for stories**. Stories are extremely powerful — our brain
often thinks in stories, understands them easily, and remembers them far better.
Because stories often create visuals in our minds,
and we tend to remember visual things much more easily. Even when it comes
to relationships, people who are good storytellers often
have much better relationships. There’s even a
book called **Storyworthy**, where the author says
that the reason his wife became his wife is because he was such a good storyteller.
He wasn’t particularly great-looking, but it was
his ability to speak — his storytelling ability — that impressed his wife.
That’s how they got married, and now he is doing really well in life, especially
when it comes to relationships. The next skill is **being optimistic**.
Again, there are two types of people: One type — no matter what solution you give
them, they will always show you a problem in it. And the other type — no matter
how many problems you give them, they will always guide you toward a solution.
The second type of people I just mentioned are usually **optimistic**, and if you
notice, the optimistic people are
the ones who **create history**. They are the ones who change the world.
For example, if there’s a lot of corruption
in the world, and I become **pessimistic**, thinking “no
matter what I do, nothing will change,” then will I be able to do anything? No.
If my emotions become negative,
and my energy turns negative, I won’t feel like doing anything.
I won’t feel like improving myself, the system, or the world. But optimistic
people are different — they know that yes, there are many
problems and a lot of corruption, **but still, we can do something about it.**
“Let’s do something.
If I try this, maybe a few small changes will happen.”
Optimistic people **dream**, and often they move toward their dreams.
Their dreams don’t get fully realized every time, but when some of their dreams
do come true, they **make history**. That’s why it’s important to always focus
on **being optimistic**. The next skill you should learn is **confidence**.
I’ve noticed a common pattern among many successful people: the successful ones are
usually **very confident**. Have you ever seen a video where a person — just
an individual — is very confident, even though they are saying
something completely wrong, but still, their
videos get **millions of views**, and a lot of people appreciate them?
Whereas you might have seen someone say something very intelligent, but
their content doesn’t get many views — why?
Because they didn’t speak it with enough **confidence**. As a content
creator, I see this every day, all the time. It’s not just about virality.
If you want money in life, again, you need **confidence** — the belief
that yes, you **can create a company** or achieve something significant.
“Yes, I can take my company to the next level. Yes, my work has value.
I have the ability.” Until you have **self-confidence**, you won’t be able
to give your 100% to any task. That’s why it’s essential to **develop the
skill of confidence** in your life. The next skill is one that has **helped
me a lot**…
Personally, for me, it’s **content creation**.
As Tanmay Bhatt says, content creation gives
you **asymmetric returns**. That means if you post one video, it’s not
like you’ll get 2x or 3x returns. It’s possible that one piece of content could
give you **100x returns**. You never know which video will go viral, or even if
it doesn’t, maybe out of the
100 people who saw your video, **one of them could be a very big investor**.
They watched your video, liked
your idea — or maybe liked you — and a connection was made.
They might even invest in your business. The **possibilities are basically
endless**. When you create content, you get money, respect, and freedom —
all great things. But along with that, there’s another amazing benefit content
creation gives you: **asymmetric returns**.
It gives you connections you can’t even imagine. I see content creators
like this every day — six months or a year ago, they were nothing.
But in just six months, they’ve achieved so much growth that big companies are now
**inviting them**, paying them from their own pockets, taking
them on stage, giving them gifts, flight tickets, and hotel stays.
They are **paying them just to come and talk**.
And this is a huge opportunity. That’s why, if possible, you should **learn the
skill of content creation**. This skill has helped me grow a lot personally
in my own life. The next skill related to this is **book reading**. If I had
to name just one skill that completely
changed my life, it would be this first **good skill and habit**.
In books, there are hidden gems — knowledge that, if you learn it, can
help you **solve any problem in your life**. In fact, I often
say that if you have any problem in your life, trust me — **someone,
somewhere has already faced that
problem**, and the solution has already been written down in some book.
You just need to **find that book**, learn the lesson from it, and **apply it
in your life**. If you do that, you can solve **any problem** in your life —
whether it’s about earning money, overcoming an illness, improving your
relationships, or simply experiencing spirituality and happiness in your life.
The next skill is **creativity**. There was a research study that found that
in the coming times, skills like coding and communication will still be important,
but the **number
one skill** will be **creativity**. A creative person can do anything today.
I read this study many years ago, but now I can confirm it even
more — ever since AI has arrived, what you really need is **creativity**.
If you are a creative person, you can create **images
and content that grab people’s attention** — content that compels them
to give you their time or even their money. No matter what field
you are in, if you **inject creativity** into it, you can **10x your results**.
You should definitely learn this one skill in your life as well. The next skill
that will help you a lot, especially if you want to become rich
in life, is **investing**. Just earning money doesn’t make a person rich.
A person becomes rich when, after earning money,
they **invest it in the right places**. I also learned this from *Rich
Dad Poor Dad*: if you just work for money, your life will eventually be over.
After some time, you will need to **put your money to work**, and there
are many ways to do that — you can invest in stocks, real estate, and so on. But
if you don’t have a lot of money, there is **one thing you can invest in**,
and that is **your mind**. For example, when Warren Buffett was asked in
an interview what his best investment
was, he didn’t say, “My best investment was Coca-Cola or Gillette.” He said that
he bought a **communication course by Dale Carnegie**, and that
was the **best investment of his life**. Similarly, I’ve noticed that whenever I
spend money to **learn something or improve myself**, the returns I get are
usually **5x, 10x, or even 100x**. The next skill that will help you immensely
in life — I’ve personally noticed that **until I applied this skill in my own
life, or whenever I became a bit weak in this skill, it showed in my results**.
There are many problems, and the name of this skill is **emotional control**.
If you’re in business, I’ve heard businessmen say that if you want
to become a good businessman, **always keep ice on your head and sugar on your
tongue**. Meaning, stay **composed
and patient in your mind**, and keep your words **sweet and polite**.
And I think, to some extent, this is absolutely true.
**Patience** and **emotional control** are very important, because many times
what happens is: when people get overly excited, they make promises that they
often cannot fulfill, which creates
problems — whether in relationships, business, or even health. On the
other hand, when they get very angry, they make decisions… They say things
that even **hurt themselves**, waste
their **time and energy**, and also **hold them back from progressing in life**.
That’s why **controlling your emotions** is a very important skill, and you need
to achieve mastery in it. The next skill to develop is **meditation**.
I’ve talked about **meditation** many times and even made several videos on it.
I’ve explained its **scientific benefits** and shared stories of people
who, with the help of meditation, healed their illnesses and improved their lives.
But honestly, until I **practiced it myself**, it was just **theory**.
But ever since I started **meditating early in the morning**, the magic
began. Since then, I’ve been able to **control my emotions** much better.
You know how sometimes your emotions are unstable — when you start meditating, all
of that begins
to **stabilize**. The **hippocampus** in your brain also starts to grow.
The **grey matter** in your brain also starts to increase.
Overall, you can say that all the positive aspects of your brain improve — it even
reduces your **fight-or-flight response**. Your
**amygdala** begins to calm down, and many other amazing changes start happening
in your brain. There are numerous studies showing how **meditation can
help you progress significantly in life**.
So, start **meditating** right now. If you want, **pause this video** and take
a **deep breath three times**. Take a
long breath, **hold it**, and then **release**.
Do it **one more time**.
When.
once more
And if you’ve just taken **three deep breaths**, you’ll notice
something — a strange sense of **calmness** will come over you.
You’ll feel **good**.
Now, because I meditate regularly, even **three breaths right now**
have brought me into a very **productive state**, and I feel really good.
But if you don’t have the habit yet, just **practice a little**.
If you meditate, honestly, you won’t
need **any addictions** or **external things**.
Just by sitting quietly, you can **generate very good feelings within
yourself**, and you can produce **positive energy whenever you want**.
This is exactly what I do every morning as part of my **21-day challenge**.
Meditation aside, the next skill I’ve learned from many books — whether related
to the **Law of Attraction**, goals, or gaining **clarity in life** —
is **visualization**. You might have noticed that many top players,
like **Ronaldo,
Virat Kohli**, or big celebrities, strongly believe in **manifestation**.
From the **Law of Attraction** perspective, you
might understand this. But even from the **goals perspective**, until you have
**clear, meaningful goals** in your life — goals that you can **see, feel, and
hear** — you won’t achieve much. And if you don’t have them, what will happen?
You will keep **wandering**, again and again, staying **distracted**.
You won’t be able to focus.
You won’t know **what to focus on**.
You also won’t exactly know **what you want in life**. Because
if you knew with **100% certainty** what you wanted, you would find a way.
You would find
a way to **meditate, visualize, and use affirmations** to boost your energy.
The next skill you should definitely apply in your life is **self-education**.
In traditional education, we invest
a lot of **time and money**, but how much **return** do we actually get?
You can comment and let me know — from your studies, how much return did
you get? If I tell you about myself, the return I got was **zero**.
For example, I did engineering, but I couldn’t earn more money from it.
It’s a different matter that I didn’t dive in much.
Even for those who did, I noticed they started
with only around 10,000–15,000. Meanwhile, with
content creation, I started earning **lakhs of rupees** in just a few years.
That made me realize that **traditional education
is perhaps far behind**.
It’s not that it’s completely bad, but it **has many flaws**.
Whereas **self-education**
is always very powerful in today’s time, because in self-education, you do what
**your mind wants**. When you educate yourself, you learn things that **you are
passionate about, that you are good at, and that you believe will
work**. That’s why **self-education is a very powerful skill**.
The next skill is **adaptability**, which is also a very powerful skill. I made
a video called *Who
Moved My Cheese*, where I shared the full story — you should check out that video.
But the **crux** is this: if you are **not changing in your life**,
if you are **not adapting to the times**, you will get left behind.
Here’s a very famous example that people often give: **Nokia**
was once the biggest mobile phone company.
Everyone had a Nokia phone.
But when **Android** came, Nokia took too long to adopt the new
systems that people had already started using.
As a result, **Nokia fell behind**.
If you don’t want your story to have a **twist like Nokia’s**, there’s
one thing you must keep doing: **be adaptable**.
For example, the best example right now is that **we are in the era of AI**.
And honestly, I have **a lot of confidence** in this.
Just like 10 years ago I had strong belief in content creation, today
I am very confident that **AI will advance significantly in the coming times**.
Start **using all these AI-related tools**.
Try to **automate your work**. If you keep learning this skill, even just a
little at a time, you can become **much richer in the future**
and advance by being highly **adaptive**. The next skill is **networking**.
Look, even if you have excellent skills, but you are **stuck in just one place**…
If you’re not **meeting people**, you will fall far behind. Over the last
10 years, in content
creation or in the industry, I’ve noticed that if there are **two people with equal
talent**, or even if they’re not equal — one person is very talented, and the other
is slightly less talented — the **less talented person…**
…who has **very good connections**. So, this **less talented person** can still
earn **more than the more talented person**.
They get many more **opportunities**. For good networking, I’ll give you a
**protective tip**: never network with the mindset of, “I’ll meet this person and
think about what I can get from them.” Don’t network with the mindset of taking.
If you want to network, always think about, **“What can I give to the other
person?
How can I provide value?”** If you meet someone and can say, **“I can provide
this value to you, this can benefit you,”** that person will want
to **connect with you**.
The next skill is the **ability to not give up**. If you have a clear
goal and your **vision is clear** — you know exactly what you want and are
fully focused on it — and if you’ve learned how
to **pursue it relentlessly**, the entire universe will eventually **align
to help you achieve it**. All you need is **passion** and **dedication**.
You just need to work **consistently**.
And to achieve consistency, there’s one more thing: **being persistent**.
A persistent person is someone who, if they go to sell something
to a person and get **rejected**, they might feel upset or even cry.
But then they go to another person to sell it.
If rejected again, they go to a third person.
Or even with the **same person, they’ll try 100 times**.
Being **persistent** means doing the same work **over
and over again**, even when most people don’t have the stamina to keep going.
If you learn this skill — **to be persistent** in your work — you can
become **super, super rich, successful, and happy**.
Another skill I want to share with you is to **have some physical activity**.
You must develop at least **one skill in your life that includes a physical
activity element**. Because nowadays, do you know what the biggest problem is?
People are **overusing the things they should use less**, and **underusing the
things they should use more**. People are overusing their
**brains**, which is causing **overthinking, anxiety,
panic attacks**, and all sorts of other problems.
Depression — while if you **move your body more, stay active, and take action**,
the pressure will reduce and
you’ll get **better results**. You might have heard about **Jeff Bezos**.
Stress doesn’t come from having a lot of work.
Stress comes when you have a lot of work, **but you’re not doing a single thing**.
And this is something I’ll tell you **right now**.
For example, just yesterday I had to leave — I’m going out of India — and I had
**a lot of work**. As long as I was **just thinking about those tasks**,
I felt **pressure**.
But now, as I’m **making this video and working**, I **don’t feel stressed**. I
am **feeling good**. This is the **best testimony** that this lesson is true.
Don’t just overthink — **take action**.
For me, making this video was an action. I’m giving you an action too.
